thrilling.def: causing great excitement and a strong happy feeling
thrilling.ex: It was a thrilling match when the school team scored in the last minute.

throw away.def: to put something in the bin because it is not needed
throw away.ex: Please do not throw away your food tray before returning it to the counter.

thunder.def: the loud booming sound heard during a storm
thunder.ex: The baby woke up and cried when a loud clap of thunder shook the windows.

thunderous.def: extremely loud like the booming sound of a storm
thunderous.ex: The crowd gave a thunderous cheer when the school team scored the winning goal.

ticket.def: a small piece of paper that lets you enter a place or event
ticket.ex: Mum bought a ticket for the family to watch the circus on Saturday afternoon.

tidier.def: more neat and well arranged than before
tidier.ex: After cleaning up, the classroom looked much tidier than it did in the morning.

tidy.def: neat and arranged in a proper orderly way
tidy.ex: The librarian kept the bookshelves tidy so students could find books easily.

tidy up.def: to make a place neat and clean by putting things away
tidy up.ex: The children helped to tidy up the living room before their grandparents arrived.

tilled.def: dug and turned over the ground to prepare it for growing plants
tilled.ex: The old man tilled his small garden plot every morning before breakfast.

timid.def: easily frightened and not confident around others
timid.ex: The new puppy was very timid and hid behind the sofa when strangers arrived.

tiny.ex: A tiny ant carried a large crumb of bread all the way across the playground.

tiptoed.def: walked very quietly on the tips of your toes
tiptoed.ex: The boy tiptoed past his baby sister so she stayed asleep.

tired.def: needing rest because you have no energy left
tired.ex: After the long swim, the children felt too tired to walk home.

tiring.def: making you feel like you need to rest
tiring.ex: Carrying heavy bags up the stairs all day was very tiring.

to.def: a word showing direction or purpose toward something
to.ex: She walked to the library after school to borrow a book.

told.def: said something to someone so they would know it
told.ex: Father told the children to wash their hands before dinner.

too.def: more than is needed or wanted
too.ex: The soup was too hot for the boy to drink right away.

took.def: moved or carried something from one place to another
took.ex: She took her younger brother by the hand as they crossed the road.

took away.def: removed something or someone from a place
took away.ex: The teacher took away the phone because it rang during class.

took off.def: removed something that was being worn
took off.ex: The children took off their muddy shoes before entering the classroom.

tore.def: pulled something apart so it ripped into pieces
tore.ex: The puppy tore the corner of the homework sheet while playing.

tossed.def: threw something lightly through the air
tossed.ex: The boy tossed the ball gently to his little sister across the garden.

traditional.def: done in the old way that people have followed for a long time
traditional.ex: Grandma wore a traditional dress to the family reunion celebration.

traditions.def: customs and ways of doing things passed down over many years
traditions.ex: Our family keeps many traditions alive during the Lunar New Year.

transformed.def: changed completely into something very different
transformed.ex: The students transformed the empty classroom into a colorful art gallery.

transition.def: a change from one state or place to another
transition.ex: The move from primary school to secondary school is a big transition.

transmit.def: send or pass something from one place or person to another
transmit.ex: Mosquitoes can transmit certain illnesses from one person to another.

travel guide.def: a book or person that gives information about a place to visit
travel guide.ex: Mother read a travel guide before our family holiday in Japan.

treasure.def: care about something very much and keep it safe
treasure.ex: She will always treasure the birthday card her best friend made for her.

treasured.def: cared deeply about something and kept it very safe
treasured.ex: He treasured the small stone he found on his first camping trip.

trekked.def: walked a long and difficult journey through rough land
trekked.ex: The class trekked up the steep hill to reach the nature reserve.

trembled.def: shook in a quick and small way because of fear or cold
trembled.ex: The little cat trembled in the corner during the loud thunderstorm.

tried.def: made an effort to do something
tried.ex: The boy tried his best to finish the art project before the bell rang.

triumph.def: a great win or success after working very hard
triumph.ex: Winning the relay race was a huge triumph for the whole team.

trivial.def: not important or serious at all
trivial.ex: The argument over who sat by the window seemed trivial to the teacher.

trolley.def: a small cart on wheels used to carry things
trolley.ex: Mother put all the groceries into the trolley at the supermarket.

trophy.def: a cup or model given as a prize for winning something
trophy.ex: The captain held up the golden trophy after the school won the match.

trust.def: a strong belief that someone is honest and will not let you down
trust.ex: The dog showed great trust by following its owner everywhere.

trustworthy.def: able to be relied on to be honest and do the right thing
trustworthy.ex: A good friend is always trustworthy and keeps your secrets safe.

try out.def: test something new to see if you like it or if it works
try out.ex: The children wanted to try out the new board game after dinner.

tumbled.def: fell or rolled down in a quick and uncontrolled way
tumbled.ex: The stack of books tumbled off the desk when the cat jumped up.

turbulence.def: sudden rough and unsteady movement in air or water
turbulence.ex: The pilot asked everyone to buckle up because of strong turbulence ahead.

turn off.def: stop a machine or light from working by using a switch
turn off.ex: Please turn off the classroom lights before you leave for recess.

ugly.ex: The old broken fence looked ugly next to the neat garden.

under the weather.ex: Father stayed home because he felt under the weather that morning.

unhurt.def: not harmed or wounded in any way
unhurt.ex: The little boy fell off his bicycle but was completely unhurt.

uniform.def: a set of matching clothes worn by everyone in a group
uniform.ex: Every pupil ironed their school uniform the night before the first day.

unity.def: people working or staying together as one group
unity.ex: The assembly reminded students that unity makes the school community strong.

unknown.def: not familiar or not yet found out by anyone
unknown.ex: The author of the old poem found in the library remains unknown.

unpleasant.def: not nice and making you feel bad or uncomfortable
unpleasant.ex: The smell from the rubbish bin outside was very unpleasant on a hot day.

unravelled.def: came apart thread by thread or became clear after being puzzling
unravelled.ex: The mystery of the missing hamster unravelled when they checked behind the bookshelf.

unsettling.def: making you feel worried or uncomfortable
unsettling.ex: The loud thunder at night was unsettling for the young puppy.

unverified.def: not yet checked or shown to be true
unverified.ex: The teacher told us to ignore unverified news found online.

upload.def: to send a file from your device to the internet
upload.ex: Mei uploaded her science project to the school website last night.

upset.def: feeling sad or unhappy about something bad
upset.ex: Tom was upset when his dog ran out of the gate.

urgent.def: needing to be done or handled right away
urgent.ex: The teacher sent an urgent message to all parents about the school closure.

usual.def: happening or done most of the time normally
usual.ex: Ali woke up at his usual time and made breakfast for his family.

vaccinated.def: given a shot to protect the body from illness
vaccinated.ex: The vet vaccinated the kittens so they would not get sick.

vague.def: not clear or not giving enough detail
vague.ex: The directions to the camp were so vague that we got lost.

vaguely.def: in a way that is not clear or exact
vaguely.ex: She vaguely remembered the face of her kindergarten teacher.

valuable.def: worth a lot of money or very important
valuable.ex: Grandma kept her most valuable ring in a small wooden box.

vanish.def: to disappear suddenly so nobody can see it
vanish.ex: The rabbit seemed to vanish behind the large curtain on stage.

vanished.def: went away suddenly and could not be found
vanished.ex: The magician waved his hand and the rabbit vanished from the box.

variable.def: a thing that can change in a test or study
variable.ex: The teacher explained that temperature was the variable we would change.

vast.def: extremely large in size or amount
vast.ex: The park was so vast that we could not see the other end.

vendor.def: a person who sells things at a stall or market
vendor.ex: The vendor at the corner sold cold drinks on hot afternoons.

vendors.def: people who sell things at stalls or markets
vendors.ex: The vendors at the food fair packed up their stalls after sunset.

venom.def: poison made by some animals to hurt others
venom.ex: The doctor treated the boy quickly after snake venom entered his hand.

venomous.def: able to produce poison that harms other animals
venomous.ex: The ranger warned us to stay away from the venomous spider near the log.

very slowly.def: at an extremely low speed, taking a long time
very slowly.ex: The injured bird moved very slowly across the garden path.

very tiring.def: making you feel extremely worn out and in need of rest
very tiring.ex: Carrying heavy bags up four flights of stairs was very tiring for the boys.

veterinary.def: relating to the care and treatment of animals
veterinary.ex: My aunt works at a veterinary clinic and helps sick animals every day.

vigorous.def: done with great energy and strength
vigorous.ex: The coach led the team in a vigorous warm-up before the match.

visibility.def: how far or clearly you can see in a place
visibility.ex: The fog reduced visibility on the road so drivers turned on their lights.

visible.def: able to be seen with the eyes
visible.ex: The red kite was still visible above the tall trees in the park.

visitors.def: people who come to see a place or person for a time
visitors.ex: The visitors at the nature reserve took photos of the baby otters.

vivid.def: very bright or producing a strong clear picture
vivid.ex: The children drew vivid pictures of their favourite animals in art class.

vividly.def: in a very clear and bright way that is easy to remember
vividly.ex: Grandpa spoke vividly about the market he visited as a young boy.

volunteer.def: a person who offers to do something without being paid
volunteer.ex: A volunteer came to school every Friday to read stories to younger students.

volunteered.def: offered to do something without being forced or paid
volunteered.ex: Three students volunteered to clean up the classroom after the party.

waded.def: walked through water or something that makes moving hard
waded.ex: The children waded through the shallow stream to reach the other bank.

wagged.def: moved from side to side quickly again and again
wagged.ex: The puppy wagged its tail and ran to greet the children after school.

wait.def: to stay in a place until something happens
wait.ex: The children had to wait outside the classroom until the teacher arrived.

waited.def: stayed in a place until something happened
waited.ex: Mum waited at the school gate until she saw her son walk out.

waiting.def: staying in a place until something happens
waiting.ex: The cat sat waiting by its bowl before the owner poured in the food.

walk on.def: to keep walking and not stop along the way
walk on.ex: Even though his feet hurt, he decided to walk on to reach the shelter.

walls.def: tall flat sides of a room or building made of brick
walls.ex: The children painted bright flowers on the walls of the community centre.

warm.def: friendly and kind in a way that makes others feel good
warm.ex: The new teacher had a warm manner that made every student feel welcome.

was.def: a past form of the word meaning to exist or be something
was.ex: The little boy was very excited on the first day of school.

was a piece of cake.def: something that is very easy to do
was a piece of cake.ex: For Priya, the spelling test was a piece of cake after weeks of practice.

was very popular.def: was liked or enjoyed by a very large number of people
was very popular.ex: The new storybook was very popular and every copy sold out within a day.

wash.def: to clean something using water and soap
wash.ex: The children wash their faces every morning before school.

wash up.def: to clean plates and pots after eating a meal
wash up.ex: Tom and his sister wash up the bowls after dinner every night.

wasted.def: used something good in a careless or wrong way
wasted.ex: The boy wasted his free time and forgot to finish his homework.

watered.def: gave liquid to a plant to help it grow
watered.ex: Siti watered the sunflowers in the garden every morning.

waterfall.def: a stream of liquid that drops down over a tall rock
waterfall.ex: The children heard the loud roar of the tall waterfall nearby.

weak.def: not having much strength or power
weak.ex: The sick kitten was too weak to drink milk on its own.

weaken.def: to make something or someone less strong
weaken.ex: The long illness started to weaken the old dog over time.

weakest.def: the least strong among a group of things or people
weakest.ex: The coach helped the player improve his weakest skills each day.

weakness.def: a lack of strength or a big fault in someone
weakness.ex: The coach helped each player work on their weakness during training.

weight.def: how heavy a person or object is
weight.ex: The vet checked the puppy's weight at every monthly visit.

weird.def: very strange and not normal or expected
weird.ex: The cat made a weird sound in the middle of the night.

wellbeing.def: the state of feeling healthy and happy overall
wellbeing.ex: The teacher checked on each student's wellbeing every Friday.

went.def: moved from one place to another place
went.ex: The class went to the zoo on a sunny Friday morning.

were.def: a past form of the word used to say what things are like
were.ex: The students were very excited about the science fair last week.

wet.def: covered with water or another liquid
wet.ex: Amir came home with wet shoes after he stepped in a puddle.

where.def: used to ask or say the place of something
where.ex: The teacher asked where the students left their permission slips.

whisk.def: to stir eggs or liquid very fast with a tool
whisk.ex: Mum asked me to whisk the eggs before she added the flour.

whisper.def: to speak very softly so others nearby cannot hear
whisper.ex: The boy whispered the answer to his friend during the library session.

white.def: having the very light colour of fresh snow or milk
white.ex: The fluffy rabbit had soft white fur all over its body.

whos.def: short form of who is or who has
whos.ex: The teacher asked who's going to read the next paragraph aloud.

wicked.def: very bad and cruel to others
wicked.ex: The wicked witch in the story locked the children in a tower.

wilted.def: became limp and droopy because of heat or no water
wilted.ex: The flowers in the vase wilted after three days without fresh water.

winners.def: people who come first or succeed in a contest
winners.ex: The three class winners each received a gold medal at assembly.

wireless.def: able to connect and send signals without using cables
wireless.ex: The school set up a new device so every classroom has wireless access.

wisdom.def: good sense and knowledge gained from long experience
wisdom.ex: The old fisherman shared his wisdom with the young boys at the dock.

wisps.def: small thin bits of smoke or cloud drifting through the air
wisps.ex: Thin wisps of smoke rose from the campfire into the night sky.

withdraw.def: to pull back or move away from something
withdraw.ex: The shy boy decided to withdraw from the singing contest at school.

witness.def: to see something happen with your own eyes
witness.ex: The children got to witness a baby turtle hatching on the beach.

women.def: more than one adult female person
women.ex: The women in our school canteen cook very tasty food.

work.def: to do a job or task that takes effort
work.ex: The students work hard on their projects every afternoon after school.

worried.def: feeling uneasy because something bad might happen
worried.ex: Mum looked worried when her son did not come home after school.

writing.def: making words or letters on paper
writing.ex: Tom is writing a story about a lost puppy in the park.

wrong.ex: He copied the wrong date into his homework notebook.

wrote.def: made words on paper in the past
wrote.ex: She wrote a letter to her grandmother after the school holidays.

yield.def: to give out or produce something as a result
yield.ex: The garden plants yield fresh vegetables for the family every week.

zookeepers.def: people whose job is to look after animals at a zoo
zookeepers.ex: The zookeepers fed the elephants early every morning before visitors arrived.
